A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ANSE/BANSA research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original CogVideoX generation experiments, VBench measurements, acquisition-function comparisons and ablations, including additional experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds results for further backbones, FreqPrior comparisons, MSR-VTT motion evaluation, human preferences and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The specified masking procedure changes from Softmax(QK^T multiplied by a mask) in v1 Equation 7 to masking attention probabilities and renormalizing rows in v2 Section 3.2. This locally revises stochastic attention construction while retaining seed minimization, single-step scoring and layer truncation. However, v2 Figure 3 still depicts the old construction, leaving implementation ambiguity. The score-sign correction alone does not establish changed selection behavior: v1's appendix already specifies the positive implementation.

E1.justification: V2 adds MSR-VTT test captions and corresponding real reference videos for motion evaluation (Table 6). This extends data coverage within the existing text-to-video task; VBench-long remains the principal benchmark. Additional model backbones primarily change experimental configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V1 explicitly omits quantitative noise-prior comparisons. V2 Table 4 evaluates FreqPrior on AnimateDiff alongside vanilla generation, ANSE and FreqPrior plus ANSE, introducing a substantive external-method comparison and combination test. The random, entropy and dropout acquisition comparisons are retained. FreeInit remains discussed without a reported evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: V2 adds AnimateDiff, HunyuanVideo, Wan2.1 and IPOC-2B configurations, quality-only evaluation for HunyuanVideo/Wan2.1, and FVMD evaluation using 200 MSR-VTT test prompts and real references. New controls compare CFG scales 5.0/7.5 and 50/60 sampling steps. Appendix K introduces a randomized, blinded human study with 30 prompts and 12 evaluators. The reported VBench video count changes from 4,730 to 4,750; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 4 tests cross-prompt seed transfer, attention-map consistency and latent trajectory behavior. Section 6 and Appendices G-I add masking-probability sensitivity, self- versus cross-attention analysis, CFG interaction and an equivalent-compute control; Figure 5 adds score-quality correlations. These substantially expand diagnostic evidence. The original ensemble-size, pool-size, reversed-selection, truncated-layer and temporal-scope analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 provides point estimates without comparable confidence-interval reporting. V2 newly states five evaluation repetitions and reports 95% confidence intervals from ten runs using random subsets of 100 videos (Appendix J, Tables 17-19). This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, but does not establish an increase in independent full-generation runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive backbone, comparator, motion, human-preference and diagnostic results. For example, its new MSR-VTT comparison reports Wan2.1 FVMD of 16495.59 for vanilla generation versus 14306.19 with ANSE (Table 6). Original CogVideoX aggregate quality, semantic and total scores remain unchanged. However, main-table CogVideoX-5B inference times change from 1223.5/1392.1 to 667.3/754.1 seconds for vanilla/ANSE; these unexplained revisions should not be interpreted as demonstrated speedups under identical conditions.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the main BANSA and BANSA-E definitions to entropy of the mean minus mean entropy, matching v1's appendix implementation and proof. It removes v1's erroneous assertion that negating scores preserves their ordering. Proposition 1 and its Jensen-inequality proof are retained, so this is a localized mathematical correction rather than new theory. Figure 3 still contains the old sign.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a training-free, model-aware noise-selection framework using attention uncertainty, efficient Bernoulli approximation and layer truncation to improve video quality and alignment with modest overhead. V2's broader experiments support the existing generality claim; the abstract's generalized backbone and overhead wording does not materially redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly interprets seed quality as prompt-dependent and connects selection to attention stability, smoother latent trajectories and expressiveness. Appendices G-I add interpretations concerning attention type, CFG interaction and benefits beyond additional computation. The discussion adds compatibility with preference refinement and proposed Self-Forcing integration. Existing failure limitations remain, while v1's explicit caveat about possible BANSA-E bias is removed.

D1.justification: V2 supplies additional configuration details: 480p Wan2.1 and 360p HunyuanVideo evaluation, 50 sampling steps for the added backbones, and layer cutoffs of 10 for AnimateDiff and approximately 20 for HunyuanVideo/Wan2.1. Existing H100 hardware, noise-pool and masking settings, score-normalization instructions, project-page link and promised future prompt-list release are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for FVMD, MSR-VTT, iterative preference optimization and Self-Forcing, and discusses complementary relationships with noise priors and post-training refinement. The central positioning relative to BALD and prior noise-initialization methods remains. Switching from numbered to author-year citations is a presentation change.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, preliminaries, methods, experiments and conclusion are rewritten or condensed. V2 introduces a dedicated noise-analysis section before experiments and reorganizes the appendix roadmap, removing the separate sign-convention discussion. Affiliation, acknowledgement and publication-header text also change. The editorial revision extends well beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: V2 adds numerous comparison, diagnostic and confidence-interval tables, a combined human-preference/correlation figure, and qualitative grids for additional backbones. Figure 4 replaces two CogVideoX examples with Wan2.1 examples. The original layer-correlation and noise-pool plots are retained but moved to appendix Figures 7-8; other original qualitative figures are also retained. The document adopts an ICLR layout with revised typography and headers.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's lack of an evaluated external noise-prior baseline and quantified uncertainty or human validation. Broader backbone tests, motion evaluation and compute/attention controls materially strengthen the evidence for generality and the proposed mechanism. Correcting the main score equations also improves mathematical clarity. Figure 3 still conflicts with the revised formulas, and the timing revisions and parts of the user-study protocol remain underexplained, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in comparative and diagnostic evidence.
